questions.q: Why is the Glue Data Catalog described as a 'shared' metadata store?
options: Athena, Redshift Spectrum, EMR, and Glue jobs can all read the same registered table without maintaining separate copies of the schema
It is only accessible from within a single Glue job at a time
Each AWS service maintains its own private copy synced from the Catalog
It is shared only between two specific IAM users
questions.explain: One Catalog table registration is visible to every compatible engine — Athena, Redshift Spectrum, EMR, and Glue jobs all read the same metadata.

questions.q: In the Data Catalog's hierarchy, what is a 'database'?
options: A logical namespace that groups related tables — not a physical database
A physical relational database that stores the actual row data
A synonym for an S3 bucket
A single partition within a table
questions.explain: Catalog 'databases' are just logical groupings of tables; no actual data or physical database engine is involved.

options: A value within a table that maps to a specific S3 sub-prefix
A physically separate copy of the table's data stored redundantly
A backup snapshot of a table's schema
A user permission level applied to a table
questions.explain: Partitions map table values (like year/month) to specific S3 prefixes, without storing any data themselves.

questions.q: What does 'schema on read' mean, as this lesson explains it?
options: Schema is applied at query time by the Catalog, while the underlying S3 files stay untyped bytes
Every row must be validated against a schema before it can be written to S3
Schema is baked permanently into each Parquet file and can never change
It means S3 enforces column types itself
questions.explain: Schema on read means structure is layered on top of raw S3 data at query time, rather than enforced when the data was written.

questions.q: What do Data Catalog databases, tables, and partitions actually store?
options: Only pointers and metadata describing where data lives in S3 and its shape — never the actual data
A full compressed copy of every table's data
Only column names, with no location or format information
IAM credentials for accessing the underlying S3 bucket
questions.explain: None of the Catalog's hierarchy levels store actual data — only metadata pointing at S3 locations and describing structure.
